q1_issues.issue: 'the climactic battle of the Mahabharata' is mapped to Possession, but the genitive section decides by ONE test — is the possessed a part / component of the possessor — and the climactic battle is an episode of the epic, which selects PartOf.

q2_gaps: a naming / appositive genitive 'the <kind> of <ProperName>' ('the battlefield of Kurukshetra'), where the proper name may name that very entity — the adjacent form ('the Brindle estuary' => one symbol plus a kind atom) and the possessive of-phrase are covered, but nothing decides between one named entity typed 'battlefield' and two entities joined by LocatedIn
an of-phrase naming what a work depicts or is about — explicitly excluded from the possessive mapping ('a photo of Mary') with no alternative encoding given
notes: 'takes place' is handled correctly as a light verb over an event-noun (no separate occur event, Location attached straight to the battle witness), the simple present correctly gets no tense atom with no TODAY and no future adjunct, and 'climactic battle' is correctly left unfused as two atoms.
